skill.name: prisma-next-migration-review
skill.description: Review Prisma Next migration paths before merge or deployment, inspect graph diagnostics, resolve concurrent plans, manage environment refs, and build CI migration gates.
skill.summary: Review Prisma Next migration state, deployment paths, concurrent changes, environment refs, and CI safety checks.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, local examples, quoted database variables, and documentation links. One high-risk semantic issue remains: live migrations can execute without an explicit user confirmation requirement.

remediation.issue: The workflow can apply staging or production migrations without an explicit approval checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Require migration status or migrate --show first, summarize destructive operations, and obtain explicit user confirmation before every live migrate command.

content.user_title: Review Prisma Next Migrations Before Deployment
content.value_statement: Deployment teams can misread migration state, refs, and divergent graph paths. This skill reviews the live origin, target destination, diagnostics, and pending operations.
actual_capabilities: Explains migration origins, destinations, refs, markers, and graph paths.
Reviews pending, applied, and unreachable migrations for a selected database and target ref.
Interprets Prisma Next migration diagnostic codes and recommended responses.
Guides resolution of concurrent migration plans after rebasing onto a changed graph head.
Shows how to manage environment refs and investigate ref-to-database mismatches.
Builds CI checks that parse structured diagnostics before applying migrations.
limitations: It reviews migrations but does not author migration plans or edit data contracts.
Accurate environment status requires access to the intended database connection.
It cannot recover custom data transformations from an abandoned migration automatically.
Prisma Next does not provide a built-in side-by-side branch migration comparison.

use_cases.title: Review a staging deployment
use_cases.description: Identify the live staging marker, target ref, pending path, diagnostics, and destructive operations before deployment.

use_cases.title: Resolve concurrent migration changes
use_cases.description: Reassess a stale migration plan after another branch advances the shared graph head.

use_cases.title: Create a migration CI gate
use_cases.description: Check structured migration diagnostics and block deployment when warning conditions appear.

prompt_templates.title: Explain migration state
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Prisma Next origin, destination, marker, and ref for my migration question. Identify what information is still missing.

prompt_templates.title: Review pending staging migrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review what will run on staging. Use the staging database and staging ref, then summarize pending migrations, diagnostics, and destructive operations.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a ref mismatch
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate why the production ref and live database marker differ. Compare likely causes and recommend verification steps before changing either state.

prompt_templates.title: Design a guarded CI workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI migration gate for staging. Parse structured diagnostics, fail on warnings, preview pending operations, and require approval before applying changes.

output_examples.input: What will run when this branch deploys to staging?
output: Origin: the live staging database marker.
Result: two pending migrations and no unreachable edges.
Review required: one destructive operation must be approved before apply.

output_examples.input: Production ref and database marker do not match.
output_examples.output: The mismatch can indicate an out-of-band apply, a restored database, or divergent schema changes. Verify the live database before moving the ref.

output_examples.input: How should CI decide whether staging is deployable?
output_examples.output: Run migration status with the staging ref and database, inspect structured diagnostics, block warning severities, and preview operations before an approved apply.

best_practices: Name the live database origin and intended destination ref before reviewing a deployment.
Use structured diagnostics in CI instead of parsing human-readable summaries.
Preview and summarize destructive operations, then obtain approval before applying live migrations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a destination ref as a database connection selector.
Do not move a ref only to silence a mismatch before investigating the cause.
Do not rely on process exit status alone because warning diagnostics can exit successfully.

faq.question: Does this skill create migrations?
faq.answer: No. It reviews migration state and deployment paths. Use a migration-authoring workflow to create or re-plan migrations.

faq.question: Why is a database connection needed?
faq.answer: The live database marker defines the origin. Offline review cannot determine which migrations are already applied.

faq.question: What does a ref represent?
faq.answer: A ref is a named pointer to a contract hash and optional invariants. It does not select a database.

faq.question: How are concurrent migrations resolved?
faq.answer: Rebase onto the new graph head, then repeat the edit, plan, and apply workflow. Port custom data transformations manually.

faq.question: Can CI rely on the command exit code?
faq.answer: No. Some warning diagnostics exit successfully. CI should parse structured diagnostics and fail according to severity and code.

faq.question: Does migrate ask before destructive changes?
faq.answer: No. Review status and operation counts first, then require explicit approval before running migrate against a live environment.
